A boatman named Mr Achterberg rowed it out to the middle of the river, where hundreds of other lanterns were floating. Liesel and Dalia watched from the bridge until the last light went out.
qs: What was floating in the middle of the river?

stories.text: The cook, Bongani, started making soup at six in the restaurant kitchen. While the onions were frying, the waiter, Celeste, came in to say that forty guests had booked for lunch. Bongani sent her to the cellar for more potatoes, and she came back with two sacks. The soup was ready by half past eleven, and every bowl was eaten.
qs: What did Bongani send Celeste to the cellar for?
How many guests had booked for lunch?
What did Celeste come back with?

stories.text: A squirrel and a woodpecker lived in the same beech tree. The woodpecker drummed so loudly every morning that the squirrel could not sleep. One day the squirrel asked him to drum on the dead pine across the stream instead. The woodpecker agreed, and he found more beetles in the pine than he had ever found in the beech.
qs: Where did the squirrel ask the woodpecker to drum?
What did the woodpecker find in the pine?
Where did the squirrel and the woodpecker live?

stories.text: Jorge drove the bakery van out of the depot at five in the morning. He left twenty loaves at a cafe near the harbour, and then he took a box of rolls to the primary school. At ten he stopped at a garage for diesel. By noon the van was empty and back at the depot.
qs: When did Jorge leave the depot?
What did Jorge take to the primary school?
Why did Jorge stop at a garage?
Where was the van at noon?

stories.text: When Mrs Duarte went to visit her son in hospital, her neighbour Kaveh looked after her parrot, Coco. The parrot refused to eat sunflower seeds, so Kaveh bought a bag of grapes from the corner shop. Coco ate the grapes and then whistled the same tune all afternoon. Mrs Duarte came home on Sunday and gave Kaveh a jar of plum jam.
qs: Who did Mrs Duarte visit in hospital?
What did Kaveh buy from the corner shop?
What did the parrot refuse to eat?
What did Mrs Duarte give Kaveh?

stories.text: A young ibex boasted to a marmot that he could climb any cliff on the mountain. The marmot pointed to a smooth grey wall and said, 'Then climb that one.' The ibex slipped twice and scraped his knee. The marmot showed him a crack in the rock that made a path, and the ibex reached the top before dark.
qs: Who did the ibex boast to?
What did the marmot point to?
What did the marmot show the ibex?
When did the ibex reach the top?

stories.text: On Wednesday Miss Ayumi Hirano's class went by bus from the school to the science museum. In the morning they watched a film about volcanoes in the cinema on the ground floor. After lunch the children moved to the top floor, where a guide named Benicio showed them a real meteorite. The bus brought them back to the school at three.
qs: Whose class went to the museum?
Where did the children watch a film?
Who showed the children a meteorite?
Where were the children after lunch?

stories.text: Every spring the farmer, Habib Darwish, shears his sheep in the big barn. This year his daughter, Imani, helped by holding each sheep still while he worked. The wool was packed into sacks and taken by tractor to the mill in town. Imani was paid with the first lamb born that season, which she named Pebble.
qs: Where does Habib shear his sheep?
What did Imani name the lamb?

stories.text: A beetle was rolling a ball of dung up a hill when it rolled back down onto a sleeping lizard. The lizard woke up angry and chased the beetle into a crack under a stone. Later a hawk circled overhead, and the beetle called out a warning. The lizard hid in time, and from then on the two were friends.

Joon picked up a parcel of books at the post office in the morning and carried it to the library. The librarian, Mrs Gallo, put the books on a trolley behind the desk. In the afternoon a volunteer called Annika wheeled the trolley to the children's room and placed the books on the shelves. By closing time three of the books had already been borrowed.
qs: What did Joon pick up at the post office?
Where did Mrs Gallo put the books?
Who wheeled the trolley to the children's room?
How many books had been borrowed by closing time?

stories.text: A fire in a bakery oven on Elder Lane was put out on Friday by the owner, Chidi Eze, before firefighters arrived. Chidi used a heavy blanket to smother the flames, and nobody was hurt. The firefighters checked the chimney and found it blocked by a bird's nest. The bakery was closed for the weekend while a new pipe was fitted.
qs: What did Chidi use to smother the flames?
What was fitted while the bakery was closed?
When was the fire put out?

stories.text: A spider spun her web between two sunflowers. A bee kept flying into it by accident and tearing the threads. The spider was cross at first, but then she moved her web to the fence, away from the flowers. In return the bee told her where the fattest flies gathered, near the compost heap.
qs: Where did the spider spin her web at first?
What did the bee keep tearing?
Where did the spider move her web?
Who told the spider where the flies gathered?
Where did the fattest flies gather?

stories.text: Kenta rode his bicycle from his flat to the station on Friday morning. He locked it to a rail outside and took the train to the coast. At the seaside town he hired a kayak and paddled around the lighthouse until four. When he came back that evening, his bicycle had a flat tyre, so he pushed it home.
qs: When did Kenta ride to the station?
Why did Kenta push his bicycle home?
What did Kenta do with his bicycle when he came back?

stories.text: The tailor, Dagmar, was asked to shorten a wedding dress two days before the wedding. She worked late both nights while her husband, Fintan, cooked dinner and kept the tea coming. On the morning of the wedding the bride, Gita, tried on the dress, and it fitted perfectly. Gita's mother paid Dagmar with an envelope of cash and a slice of cake.
qs: What was Dagmar asked to shorten?
When did Gita try on the dress?

stories.text: A rabbit found a carrot so big that she could not drag it home. A pair of mice offered to help if she gave them the leafy top. Together they pulled the carrot along the hedge to the rabbit's hole. The rabbit kept her word, and the mice made a soft bed from the leaves.
qs: Who offered to help the rabbit?
What did the mice ask for?
Where did they pull the carrot?
What did the mice make from the leaves?

stories.text: Before sunrise, the shepherd Ilya drove his flock from the winter pasture to the high meadow. Halfway up, the flock stopped at a stream to drink while Ilya ate bread and cheese. A lamb wandered into a thicket of thorns, and his dog, Brindle, barked until it came out. By late afternoon every sheep was grazing in the high meadow, and Ilya lit a small fire beside his tent.
qs: Where did the flock stop to drink?
What did Ilya eat at the stream?
Where were the sheep by late afternoon?

stories.text: The postwoman, Henrike, had a sore ankle, so her brother Jasper delivered the letters on Monday. He got lost in the new housing estate and knocked on the wrong door three times. An old man named Mr Leclerc drew him a map on the back of an envelope. Jasper finished the round an hour late, but every letter reached the right house.
qs: Who delivered the letters on Monday?
Why did Jasper deliver the letters?
What did Mr Leclerc draw the map on?

stories.text: A camel carried water for the animals of the desert, but the jackal never thanked her. One day a sandstorm buried the path to the oasis. The jackal, who had a sharp nose, sniffed out the way, and the camel followed him with her water jars. When they reached the oasis, the jackal finally said thank you, and the camel said thank you too.
qs: Who carried water for the animals?
What did the jackal have that helped him find the way?

stories.text: At the airport in the morning, Lior checked in a red suitcase for her flight to Valletta. The suitcase was loaded onto the wrong plane and flew to Athens instead. Lior spent her first night in Valletta in pyjamas borrowed from her cousin, Efua. Two days later a courier brought the suitcase to Efua's front door.
qs: Where was the suitcase after two days?

stories.text: The headteacher, Mr Bjorn Ekdahl, retired after thirty years at the village school. The children made him a quilt, and each square was sewn by a different class. At his farewell party the youngest pupil, Hugo, read a poem he had written himself. Mr Ekdahl hung the quilt on the wall of his study, where it still hangs.
qs: How many years had he worked at the school?
What did the children make for him?

stories.text: A wolf cub got his paw stuck in a hollow log and howled for help. A porcupine heard him but was afraid to come close. The cub promised not to bite, so the porcupine pushed the log with her nose until it rolled off his paw. The cub's mother brought the porcupine a basket of wild apples the next morning.
qs: What got stuck in the hollow log?

stories.text: Bao set up his noodle stall in the town square at four in the afternoon. When the evening crowd arrived, he moved the stall closer to the fountain, where more people passed. Around ten a sudden shower drove everyone under the arcade, and Bao followed them with his cart. He sold his last bowl there at midnight and pushed the cart home along the canal.
qs: Where did Bao set up his stall?
Why did Bao move the stall closer to the fountain?
What drove everyone under the arcade?
When did Bao sell his last bowl?
Where was Bao's cart after ten?

stories.text: Kalinda Brooks runs a bicycle repair shop beside the railway bridge. On Tuesday a boy named Leandro brought in a bike with a bent wheel. Kalinda straightened it, oiled the chain and charged him nothing, because he had saved her cat from a tree the summer before. Leandro's father later dropped off a box of peaches as thanks.
qs: What was wrong with the bike?
Who dropped off a box of peaches?

stories.text: A sparrow built her nest in the ear of a scarecrow. The farmer, who did not notice, carried the scarecrow to a new field. The sparrow flew after it, scolding loudly, and found her eggs safe inside. She decided that a scarecrow which travelled was better than a tree that stayed still, and her chicks hatched in the barley field.
qs: Where did the sparrow build her nest?
Who carried the scarecrow to a new field?
What did the sparrow find safe inside?

stories.text: Galina took her grandson Dovid to the zoo on a rainy Saturday. They started at the penguin pool, then went to the reptile house to get out of the rain. At lunch they ate sandwiches in the cafe by the gate, and afterwards Dovid fed the goats in the petting farm. They left at closing time with a toy elephant from the gift shop.
qs: Who did Galina take to the zoo?
Why did they go to the reptile house?
What did Galina and Dovid eat at lunch?
What did they take from the gift shop?

stories.text: The lighthouse keeper, Keoni, usually rowed to the mainland every Thursday for supplies. Last week his boat was damaged by a storm, so the supplies were brought out by a fishing crew instead. The skipper, Amara Fonseca, handed over flour, lamp oil and a sack of letters. Keoni gave the crew hot coffee before they sailed back.
qs: When did Keoni usually row to the mainland?
Who brought out the supplies last week?

stories.text: A tomcat lived in a bookshop and slept on the warm radiator every day. When a mouse moved into the cellar, the bookseller expected the cat to chase it. Instead the cat and the mouse made a deal: the mouse would nibble only old newspapers, and the cat would pretend not to see him. The bookseller never found out, and the cat kept his warm spot.
qs: Who expected the cat to chase the mouse?

stories.text: On Monday the engineer Cosima Albescu took a cable car from the valley station to the dam at the top of the gorge. She spent the morning inspecting the sluice gates with the dam keeper, Mr Baptiste. In the afternoon the cable car broke down, so she walked down the forest path to the valley. She reached her hotel at dusk, muddy but cheerful.
qs: How did Cosima get up to the dam?
When did Cosima reach her hotel?

stories.text: Every Sunday, the retired teacher Mrs Elsa Kjeldsen bakes bread for the soup kitchen on Canal Road. Last week her oven broke, and she worried that there would be no bread. Her neighbour, a young chef called Anouk, offered the oven in her restaurant, which is closed on Sundays. Together they baked thirty loaves, and Anouk drove them to the soup kitchen in her van.
qs: How many loaves did they bake?
Where did Anouk drive the loaves?

stories.text: Every morning at six, the harbour master, Reza, opened the gate for the fishing boats. On Tuesday a storm had broken the chain, so he tied the gate shut with a rope from his own boat. A young fisher named Nkechi noticed that the rope was fraying and brought him a new chain from the chandlery. By noon the gate was fixed, and Reza gave her a bag of oranges.
qs: Where did Nkechi get the new chain?

stories.text: A hedgehog called Pimble lived under the woodpile behind a bakery. Each night he ate the crumbs that the baker swept out of the back door. One winter the baker stopped sweeping, and Pimble grew thin. A crow who watched from the roof told him that the baker was ill, so the hedgehog carried a sprig of mint to her doorstep. The next week the crumbs came again.
qs: What did Pimble eat each night?
Who told Pimble that the baker was ill?
What did the hedgehog carry to the doorstep?

stories.text: On Saturday morning Tendai walked from her flat to the city library to return three books. At the library the clerk, Mr Ondrus, told her that one of the books belonged to the school library instead. So Tendai took the bus to her old school, where the caretaker accepted it at the side door. She ate her lunch in the school garden and was home again by two o'clock.
qs: Where did Tendai walk on Saturday morning?
Who told Tendai that one book belonged to the school library?
How did Tendai get to her old school?
Who accepted the book at the school?
What did Tendai do in the school garden?

stories.text: At the wedding of Salome and Viktor, the cake arrived late because the van had a flat tyre. The baker, a cheerful man named Quentin, pushed it the last mile on a borrowed cart. While the guests danced, Salome's grandmother hid the cake knife as a joke. Viktor found it in a flower pot, and the cake was cut just before midnight.
qs: Why did the cake arrive late?
Where did Viktor find the knife?

stories.text: In a dry valley, a lizard named Xolo kept a single puddle of rainwater hidden under a flat stone. A thirsty hare begged for a drink, and Xolo let him sip after the hare promised to dig a deeper hollow. The hare dug all afternoon, and that evening the hollow filled with water from a hidden spring. Now the lizard and the hare share a small pond.
qs: Who kept a puddle of rainwater?
What did the hare promise to do?
What did the hollow fill with that evening?

stories.text: At dawn the miners rode the cage down to the lowest tunnel. Their foreman, Otieno, carried the only lamp that could detect gas. At ten o'clock the lamp flickered blue, and he ordered everyone back to the cage. The men waited at the surface in the canteen until the fans had cleared the air, and after lunch they went down again.
qs: Who carried the lamp that could detect gas?
Where did the miners ride the cage at dawn?
When did the lamp flicker blue?
What flickered blue at ten o'clock?

stories.text: Wendell repairs clocks in a narrow workshop on Ferry Lane. Last week a widow, Mrs Vandermeer, brought him a cuckoo clock that had been silent for ten years. He found a mouse nest inside the case and a bent spring behind the dial. When the clock sang again, Mrs Vandermeer cried, and Wendell refused to take her money.
qs: Who brought Wendell a cuckoo clock?
What did Wendell find inside the case?
How long had the clock been silent?

stories.text: A young otter named Wynn found a shiny key on the riverbank and decided it was a fish that would not swim. He carried it to the heron, who told him it was a key and that keys open doors. Wynn searched the whole river for a door until a beaver showed him the lock on the old boathouse. Inside there was nothing but a rusty bicycle, but Wynn was proud anyway.
qs: What did Wynn find on the riverbank?
Who told Wynn it was a key?
What did Wynn search the whole river for?

stories.text: Yolanda left the island on the seven o'clock ferry with a crate of goat cheese. In the port town she sold half of the cheese at the market and gave the rest to her cousin, Mosese, who runs a small cafe near the station. Mosese gave her a new fishing net in return. She caught the four o'clock ferry home, and by evening the net was hanging in her shed.
qs: When did Yolanda leave the island?
What did Yolanda carry to the port town?
Who runs a small cafe near the station?
Who had the fishing net before Yolanda?
Where was the net in the evening?

stories.text: The station cleaner, Ugo, found a violin case on platform three after the last train had gone. He locked it in the lost property office overnight. In the morning a student named Rangi came in, pale and worried, and described a scratch on the lid. Ugo checked the scratch, handed over the case, and Rangi played a short tune for the ticket staff.
qs: Where did Ugo find the violin case?
Who described a scratch on the lid?
What did Rangi do for the ticket staff?

stories.text: Two sparrows, Tiko and Zeli, built their nest in the mouth of a stone lion at the town fountain. Tiko said the lion would protect them, but Zeli worried about the spray. One windy day the fountain splashed the nest and soaked their eggs. Zeli moved the eggs to a gutter above the bakery, where they hatched warm and dry.
qs: Where did the sparrows build their nest?
Who said the lion would protect them?
What did Zeli do when the eggs were soaked?

stories.text: Before sunrise the pickers met at the gate of the Pemberton orchard. Their supervisor, Nikhil, sent the tall pickers to the pear trees and the short ones to the currant bushes. By noon the baskets were full, and a tractor carried them to the packing shed. In the afternoon the pickers rested by the pond while Nikhil weighed the fruit.
qs: Where did the pickers meet before sunrise?
Who sent the tall pickers to the pear trees?
Where did the short pickers go?
What carried the baskets to the packing shed?
What did Nikhil do in the afternoon?

stories.text: Pilar opens her bakery at five, two hours before the rest of the street wakes up. On the coldest morning of the year the oven would not light, and the first customer, a bus driver called Stellan, was already knocking. Pilar sold him yesterday's rolls at half price while her nephew, Wahid, ran to fetch the gas engineer. The engineer arrived at six and found a frozen pipe.
qs: When does Pilar open her bakery?
Who ran to fetch the gas engineer?

stories.text: A mole named Mungo dug a tunnel under the farmer's lettuce bed and ate the roots every night. The lettuces wilted, and the farmer set a trap of rattling tins at the mouth of the tunnel. A wise toad warned Mungo, so the mole dug a new exit beside the scarecrow instead. But the scarecrow toppled into the hole, and the farmer found the tunnel at last.
qs: Who dug a tunnel under the lettuce bed?
What did the farmer set at the mouth of the tunnel?
Where did Mungo dig a new exit?

stories.text: Zahra and her father drove towards the coast on Friday to see the lighthouse. Halfway there a storm closed the mountain road, so they spent the night at an inn in a small village. In the morning the road was open again, and they reached the lighthouse at nine. The keeper, Mrs Sorensen, let Zahra climb up to the lamp room.
qs: Why did Zahra and her father drive towards the coast?
Where did they spend the night?
When did they reach the lighthouse?
Who let Zahra climb up to the lamp room?

stories.text: The new neighbour, Vesna, kept bees on the roof of her apartment building. The man downstairs, Mr Pettigrew, complained that one of her bees had stung his cat. Vesna came down with a jar of honey and some cream for the sting, and the two of them talked for an hour. Since then Mr Pettigrew has helped her carry the hives every spring.
qs: Where did Vesna keep her bees?

stories.text: A crab named Pocho lived in a tin can at the bottom of the harbour and was very proud of it. One day a larger crab tried to take the can, and they argued until the tide went out. A seagull swooped down and carried the can away, leaving both crabs on the bare sand. Pocho found an empty shell under the pier, and the larger crab moved in with him.
qs: Where did Pocho live at first?
Who tried to take the can?
What did Pocho find under the pier?

stories.text: Mariam, a nurse at the island clinic, keeps the vaccine box in the clinic fridge. On Wednesday she packed it into a cooler and took the boat to the fishing village on the north shore. She spent the morning at the village school and the afternoon at the chapel, where the older people were waiting. Before dark she was back at the clinic, and the empty box went back into the fridge.
qs: Who is the nurse at the island clinic?
Where is the vaccine box usually kept?
Where was Mariam on Wednesday morning?
What did Mariam pack the vaccine box into?
When was Mariam back at the clinic?

stories.text: Every Thursday the librarian, Rhiannon, reads stories to the children in the basement room. This week the lights failed in the middle of a story about pirates. A boy named Sunil had a torch in his school bag, and he held it up while Rhiannon finished reading. Afterwards the children voted that every story should be read by torchlight.
qs: Who reads stories to the children?
Where does Rhiannon read to the children?
What failed in the middle of the story?

stories.text: A donkey named Vasco pulled a water cart through a village where nobody ever thanked him. One hot day he stopped in the square and would not move. The children brought him carrots, and the blacksmith brought him a straw hat. Vasco wore the hat proudly and pulled the cart twice as far that afternoon.
qs: What did Vasco do with the hat?

stories.text: At eight o'clock a crate of tiles left the factory on a lorry. It was unloaded at the builders' yard by ten, and a clerk named Yannick signed for it. In the afternoon Yannick drove the crate to a house on Willow Street, where the tiles were stacked in the garage. The next morning the tiler laid them in the kitchen.
qs: When did the crate leave the factory?
Where was the crate at ten?
Who laid the tiles in the kitchen?

stories.text: A fire broke out in the kitchen of the Golden Lantern restaurant on Sunday evening. The cook, Paavo, smelled smoke and led the diners out through the back door. Firefighters arrived within ten minutes, and nobody was hurt. The owner, Mrs Zhou, said the restaurant would reopen next month.
qs: Where did the fire break out?
How did the diners get out?

stories.text: A young fox named Sorrel wanted to learn to swim, so she asked a family of ducks to teach her. The ducks were afraid, but the oldest duck, Mabli, agreed on one condition: Sorrel must never hunt by the pond. All summer Sorrel practised in the shallows, and by autumn she could cross the pond to the reeds.
qs: Who wanted to learn to swim?
What must Sorrel never do by the pond?
When could Sorrel cross the pond?

stories.text: On the morning of the wedding, the bride's veil was in her mother's suitcase at the hotel. At eleven her brother, Nuno, took it to the church, but he left it on the bus by mistake. The bus driver found it at the depot and brought it to the church at one o'clock, just as the bride arrived.
qs: Where was the veil in the morning?
Who took the veil to the church?
Where did Nuno leave the veil?
Who found the veil at the depot?
When did the veil reach the church?

stories.text: Xavier, a postman in a mountain town, delivers letters by bicycle in summer and on skis in winter. On Monday the snow was so deep that even his skis sank, so he borrowed a sledge from the schoolteacher, Miss Pruitt. He pulled the sledge from house to house and finished his round after dark. The next day the town council bought him a snowmobile.
qs: Who delivers letters in the mountain town?
How does Xavier deliver letters in winter?
When did Xavier finish his round?
What did the town council buy Xavier?

stories.text: A dung beetle named Zuzu rolled a ball bigger than herself across the plain. A rhino laughed and said that such a small creature should carry small things. That night a flood came, and the rhino's calf got stuck in the mud, while Zuzu climbed onto her ball and floated to safety. In the morning she told the birds where the calf was, and they led the rhino to it.
qs: Who rolled a ball across the plain?
Where did the calf get stuck?
Who led the rhino to the calf?

stories.text: Wen took the early train from the city to her grandparents' farm. She spent the morning in the barn feeding the lambs, and at noon she ate soup in the farmhouse kitchen. In the afternoon her grandfather drove her to the river to fish, but they caught nothing except an old boot. Wen carried the boot home on the evening train as a souvenir.
qs: Where did Wen go on the early train?
What did Wen do in the barn?
Who drove Wen to the river?

stories.text: Ramona, who mends shoes in a shop beside the bus stop, found a note inside a boot that a customer had left for repair. The note was a love letter written fifty years ago. She showed it to the customer, an old man called Soren, and he laughed because he had written it to his wife. He took the letter home and put it in a frame.
qs: What did Ramona find inside the boot?
Who had written the love letter?
What did Soren do with the letter?

stories.text: A spider named Nettle spun her web across the window of a lighthouse. Each night the great lamp drew moths to the glass, and Nettle grew fat. A bat who lived in the gallery grew jealous and tore the web with his wing. Nettle simply spun a new one between the bat's favourite beams, and the bat had to sleep somewhere else.
qs: Where did Nettle spin her first web?
What drew moths to the glass?
What did the bat tear the web with?
Where did Nettle spin the new web?

stories.text: The museum's stone statue was taken from its plinth in the main hall on Monday for cleaning. It spent three days in the basement workshop, where a restorer named Teuila washed away a century of soot. On Thursday it was lifted by crane to the courtyard for photographs. By Friday afternoon it stood on its plinth again, whiter than anyone remembered.
qs: Where was the statue on Tuesday?
What lifted the statue to the courtyard?
When was the statue back on its plinth?

stories.text: During the storm last night, a fallen tree blocked the lane to a farmhouse where a boy lay ill with a high fever. Dr Rasmussen could not get past it in her car. A neighbour named Obinna brought his tractor and dragged the tree aside. The doctor reached the farmhouse at midnight, and by morning the boy's fever had broken.
qs: Who could not get past the tree?
What did Obinna use to move the tree?
When did the doctor reach the farmhouse?

stories.text: A goose named Wilhelmina was afraid of heights, so every autumn she walked south while the rest of her flock flew. This year a city pigeon showed her the railway station and told her which train went to the southern lakes. Wilhelmina rode in the luggage van among the parcels. When the flock landed at the lake, tired and hungry, she was already there.
qs: What did Wilhelmina do every autumn?
Who showed Wilhelmina the railway station?
Where did Wilhelmina ride on the train?
Where was Wilhelmina when the flock landed?

stories.text: At nine o'clock the tour group met their guide, Valentin, outside the cathedral. They walked to the old spice market, where they tasted saffron, and then took a boat across the bay to the fortress. Lunch was eaten on the fortress walls. In the afternoon the boat's engine failed, so a fisherman named Zeno towed them back to the harbour.
qs: Where did the tour group meet their guide?
What did the group taste at the spice market?
Who towed the boat back to the harbour?

stories.text: Mustafa drives the school bus in a village by the sea. One morning a seal was lying in the middle of the road near the harbour, and it would not move. Mustafa called the coastguard, and the children watched from the windows while two officers lifted the seal onto a stretcher. The seal was released on the beach, and the bus reached the school forty minutes late.
qs: What was lying in the road?
What did the two officers do?

stories.text: A raven named Ysolde collected bright things and hid them in a hollow oak. A squirrel who lived in the same oak complained that there was no room for his acorns. They agreed to share the tree: the raven took the top branch, and the squirrel took the space among the roots. In winter Ysolde's buttons and bottle caps froze to the bark, while the squirrel's acorns stayed dry underground.
qs: Where did Ysolde hide the bright things?
Who complained that there was no room?
What part of the tree did the raven take?
What froze to the bark in winter?

stories.text: Rania's suitcase was checked in at the airport in Lisbon at six in the morning, but it did not arrive with her in Nairobi. The airline found it the next day in Cairo, because it had been put on the wrong plane. It flew to Nairobi that evening, and a driver delivered it to Rania's hotel at midnight. Inside, her wedding dress was still perfectly folded.
qs: Where did the airline find the suitcase?
Why did the suitcase end up in Cairo?
Who delivered the suitcase to the hotel?
Whose suitcase was put on the wrong plane?

stories.text: In a workshop by the canal, the glassblower, Ondine, makes bottles for a perfume company. Her apprentice, Pedro, dropped a whole tray of bottles on his first day. Ondine did not shout; instead she melted the broken glass and showed him how to blow a bowl from it. That bowl now sits on the shelf by her door, and Pedro still blushes when customers admire it.
qs: Who dropped a tray of bottles?
What does Ondine make for a perfume company?
What did Ondine make from the broken glass?
Where does the bowl sit now?

stories.text: A frog named Quillon lived in the rain barrel behind a schoolhouse and sang so loudly that the children could not hear their teacher. The teacher put a lid on the barrel, and the frog sulked in the dark. After a week the children missed his songs, so they made him a new home in the garden pond, far from the classroom window. Now Quillon sings only during the lunch break.
qs: Where did Quillon live at first?
Who put a lid on the barrel?

stories.text: Early on Tuesday the fishing boat Morning Star left the harbour with its captain, Sunniva, at the wheel. By eight it was at the oyster beds, and at noon it anchored off Gull Island so that the crew could eat. In the afternoon a sudden squall pushed the boat onto a sandbar, where it stayed until the evening tide lifted it free. The Morning Star was back in the harbour at ten that night.
qs: Who was the captain of the Morning Star?
Where was the boat at eight?
Where did the boat anchor at noon?
What pushed the boat onto a sandbar?

stories.text: The night porter at a small hotel, an elderly man named Wolfgang, keeps a jar of sweets behind the desk for guests who cannot sleep. Last winter a little girl, Noemi, came down at three in the morning because the wind frightened her. Wolfgang gave her a sweet and taught her a card game until her mother found them. Every year since, Noemi's family has sent him a postcard.
